children.title: SNC under Cartesian Products
children.top_down_role: Compactness preservation for product sets and product mappings.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent finite Cartesian products of set-valued mappings, with product graphs identified by a coordinate permutation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_i:X_i\rightrightarrows Y_i\) and \((\bar x_i,\bar y_i)\in\operatorname{gph}F_i\) for \(i=1,2\). Define \[F(x_1,x_2):=F_1(x_1)\times F_2(x_2).\] Under the canonical coordinate permutation, \[\operatorname{gph}F\cong\operatorname{gph}F_1\times\operatorname{gph}F_2.\] Consequently, \(F\) is sequentially normally compact at \(((\bar x_1,\bar x_2),(\bar y_1,\bar y_2))\) if and only if each \(F_i\) is sequentially normally compact at \((\bar x_i,\bar y_i)\). The equivalence extends to every finite independent Cartesian product.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An independent finite product mapping is SNC exactly when all component mappings are SNC at their corresponding graph points.
assumptions_latex: \(X_i,Y_i\) are Banach spaces and \(F_i:X_i\rightrightarrows Y_i\) for \(i=1,2\).
The finite products are equipped with standard equivalent product norms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_1\times F_2\) is SNC at the product graph point if and only if both component mappings are SNC at their graph points.
knowledge_statements.title: SNC of Independent Product Mappings

assumptions_latex: \(X,Y\) are Asplund spaces, and \(A\subset X\), \(B\subset Y\) are locally closed near \(\bar a\in A\), \(\bar b\in B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The product \(A\times B\) is SNC at \((\bar a,\bar b)\) if and only if both factors are SNC at their reference points.

notation.meaning: Cartesian product set in the product Banach space

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary Cartesian products equipped with a standard product norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Using the product-space identification \((X\times Y)^*=X^*\times Y^*\), regular normals satisfy \[\widehat N((a,b);A\times B)=\widehat N(a;A)\times\widehat N(b;B).\] Hence \[A\times B\text{ is SNC at }(\bar a,\bar b)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad A\text{ is SNC at }\bar a\text{ and }B\text{ is SNC at }\bar b.\] The reverse implication tests product normal sequences with one dual coordinate equal to zero; the forward implication applies factor SNC separately to both coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Cartesian product is SNC exactly when each factor is SNC at its corresponding reference point.
knowledge_statements.title: SNC under Cartesian Products

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The product-normal identity and SNC equivalence are plausible and precisely stated, but the record supplies no inspectable source for the direct product result.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: SNC equivalence for a two-component aggregate mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between componentwise SNC and SNC of the paired scalar mapping under qualification condition (3.80).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\varphi_i:X\to\mathbb R\), \(i=1,2\), be continuous around \(\bar x\) and satisfy qualification condition \((3.80)\). Then \(\varphi_1\) and \(\varphi_2\) are both SNC at \(\bar x\) if and only if the aggregate mapping \((\varphi_1,\varphi_2):X\to\mathbb R^2\) is SNC at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For two continuous scalar mappings satisfying qualification condition (3.80), both components are SNC exactly when their paired aggregate mapping is SNC.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \big(\varphi_1\text{ and }\varphi_2\text{ are SNC at }\bar x\big)\iff\big((\varphi_1,\varphi_2)\text{ is SNC at }\bar x\big)

children.title: Additive–Product Preservation Qualifications
children.top_down_role: Structural conditions supporting SNC across the two operation families.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is an Asplund space, \(A,B\subset X\), and \(\bar x=\bar a+\bar b\) with \(\bar a\in A\), \(\bar b\in B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Additive transversality at \((\bar a,\bar b)\) is the condition \(N(\bar a;A)\cap[-N(\bar b;B)]=\{0\}\).

notation.meaning: Addition mapping on the product space

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normal noncancellation condition at a fixed decomposition of a sum point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The additive normal qualification at the decomposition \((\bar a,\bar b)\) is \[a^*\in N(\bar a;A),\quad b^*\in N(\bar b;B),\quad a^*+b^*=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad a^*=b^*=0.\] Equivalently, \[N(\bar a;A)\cap[-N(\bar b;B)]=\{0\}.\] It rules out opposing nonzero normals at a decomposition of \(\bar x\). By contrast, Cartesian-product SNC uses coordinatewise normals and requires no cancellation qualification beyond the SNC assumptions on the factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a sum decomposition, additive transversality excludes nonzero normals to the two summands that cancel each other.
knowledge_statements.title: Additive–Product Preservation Qualifications

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The noncancellation formula is well formed, but its exact role in SNC preservation under Minkowski addition is not established. A source for the relevant addition theorem and its decomposition hypotheses is required.

children.title: Preservation Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where additive or product constructions lose normal compactness.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: A Non-SNC Factor Survives Cartesian Product with an SNC Factor
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessity of factor SNC for Cartesian-product preservation in an infinite-dimensional Hilbert factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=\ell^2\), let \((e_n)\) be its standard orthonormal basis, set \(S:=\{0\}\cup\{e_n/n:n\in\mathbb N\}\subset H\), and let \(T:=\{0\}\subset\mathbb R\). For \(s_n=e_n/n\), \(s_n\to0\), \(e_n\rightharpoonup0\), \(\|e_n\|=1\), and \(e_n\in\widehat N(s_n;S)\). Hence \(S\) is not SNC at \(0\), whereas \(T\) is SNC at \(0\). Moreover, \((e_n,0)\in\widehat N((s_n,0);S\times T)\), so \(S\times T\) is not SNC at \((0,0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Taking a Cartesian product with a finite-dimensional SNC singleton does not repair a non-SNC factor.
assumptions_latex: \(H=\ell^2\) and \((e_n)\) is its standard orthonormal basis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\) is SNC at \(0\), but \(S\times T\) is not SNC at \((0,0)\).
knowledge_statements.title: A Non-SNC Factor Survives Cartesian Product with an SNC Factor

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Neither addition nor Cartesian product can create SNC from the non-SNC factor \(S\): \(S+C=S\) and \(S\times C\) are not SNC at their origins.

notation.meaning: Standard orthonormal basis of the Hilbert space

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete boundary showing that an uncontrolled factor obstructs algebraic SNC preservation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(s_n:=e_n/n\), one has \(s_n\to0\), \(e_n	o0\) weakly, \(\|e_n\|=1\), and \(e_n\in\widehat N(s_n;S)\) because \(s_n\) is isolated. Thus \(S\) is not SNC at \(0\). Since \(S+C=S\), set addition with the neutral singleton does not remove this failure. Likewise, \((e_n,0)\in\widehat N((s_n,0);S\times C)\) converges weakly to zero but not in norm, so \(S\times C\) is not SNC at \((0,0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Addition by zero and product with a singleton retain a non-SNC factor, so algebraic constructions cannot compensate for missing factor compactness.
knowledge_statements.title: Preservation Failure Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The neutral-element examples correctly retain the non-SNC factor and fit the failure-boundary container, but no source or inspectable locator supports the nontrivial record.

children.top_down_role: Compactness preservation for composed mappings.

assumptions_latex: \(X,Y,Z\) are Asplund spaces, \(F:X\rightrightarrows Y\), \(G:Y\rightrightarrows Z\), and \(\bar y\in F(\bar x)\cap G^{-1}(\bar z)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The basic composition qualification is \(D^*G(\bar y,\bar z)(0)\cap\ker D^*F(\bar x,\bar y)=\{0\}\).

notation.meaning: Limiting coderivative of a set-valued mapping

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coderivative nondegeneracy used in SNC composition calculus.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At the intermediate point \(\bar y\), the basic coderivative qualification for composition is \[y^*\in D^*G(\bar y,\bar z)(0),
\qquad 0\in D^*F(\bar x,\bar y)(y^*)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad y^*=0.\] Equivalently, \[D^*G(\bar y,\bar z)(0)\cap\ker D^*F(\bar x,\bar y)=\{0\},\] where \(\ker D^*F(\bar x,\bar y):=\{y^*:0\in D^*F(\bar x,\bar y)(y^*)\}\). This condition excludes abnormal intermediate covectors; full SNC preservation additionally depends on the selected composition theorem's graph compactness and solution-map assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composition calculus excludes nonzero intermediate covectors that are simultaneously abnormal for the outer mapping and annihilated by the inner coderivative.
knowledge_statements.title: SNC for Mapping Compositions

knowledge_statements.statement_title: SNEC and SNC preservation under binary functional composition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compactness preservation when a lower-semicontinuous binary outer function is applied to an SNC aggregate mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\varphi_i:X\to\mathbb R\), \(i=1,2\), be continuous around \(\bar x\), set \(\bar y=(\varphi_1(\bar x),\varphi_2(\bar x))\), and let \(v:\mathbb R^2\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be lower semicontinuous around \(\bar y\). Suppose each \(\varphi_i\) is SNC at \(\bar x\) and \(\{\varphi_1,\varphi_2\}\) satisfies qualification condition \((3.80)\). Then: (i) if \(\partial^\infty v(\bar y)=\{0\}\), the function \(v(\varphi_1,\varphi_2)\) is SNEC at \(\bar x\); and (ii) if \(v\) is continuous around \(\bar y\) and \(\partial^\infty v(\bar y)\cup\partial^\infty(-v)(\bar y)=\{0\}\), then \(v(\varphi_1,\varphi_2)\) is SNC at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Applying a lower-semicontinuous binary outer function to two continuous SNC components preserves SNEC under the first singular-subdifferential condition and preserves SNC under the stronger continuity and two-sided singular-subdifferential condition.
assumptions_latex: \varphi_i\text{ is continuous around and SNC at }\bar x\text{ for }i=1,2
v:\mathbb R^2\to\overline{\mathbb R}\text{ is l.s.c. around }\bar y
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial^\infty v(\bar y)=\{0\}\Rightarrow v(\varphi_1,\varphi_2)\text{ is SNEC at }\bar x;\quad \big[v\text{ is continuous around }\bar y\land\partial^\infty v(\bar y)\cup\partial^\infty(-v)(\bar y)=\{0\}\big]\Rightarrow v(\varphi_1,\varphi_2)\text{ is SNC at }\bar x

knowledge_statements.statement_title: SNC preservation for set-valued mapping compositions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SNC preservation under inner semicompactness, complementary SNC/PSNC hypotheses, and a normal-coderivative qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar z\in(F\circ G)(\bar x)\), where \(G:X\rightrightarrows Y\) and \(F^{-1}:Z\rightrightarrows Y\) have closed graphs locally near the relevant points. Suppose \(G\cap F^{-1}\) is inner semicompact at \((\bar x,\bar z)\). For every \(\bar y\in G(\bar x)\cap F^{-1}(\bar z)\), assume either that \(G\) is PSNC at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) and \(F\) is SNC at \((\bar y,\bar z)\), or that \(G\) is SNC at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) and \(F^{-1}\) is PSNC at \((\bar z,\bar y)\). Also assume \(D_N^*F(\bar y,\bar z)(0)\cap\ker D_N^*G(\bar x,\bar y)=\{0\}\) for every such \(\bar y\). Then \(F\circ G\) is SNC at \((\bar x,\bar z)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set-valued composition is SNC when the intermediate-point mapping is inner semicompact and every relevant intermediate point satisfies both the stated complementary SNC/PSNC alternative and the normal-coderivative qualification.
assumptions_latex: G:X\rightrightarrows Y\text{ and }F^{-1}:Z\rightrightarrows Y\text{ have closed graphs locally near the relevant points}
G\cap F^{-1}\text{ is inner semicompact at }(\bar x,\bar z)

\forall\bar y\in G(\bar x)\cap F^{-1}(\bar z):\ \big[G\text{ is PSNC at }(\bar x,\bar y)\land F\text{ is SNC at }(\bar y,\bar z)\big]\lor\big[G\text{ is SNC at }(\bar x,\bar y)\land F^{-1}\text{ is PSNC at }(\bar z,\bar y)\big]
\forall\bar y\in G(\bar x)\cap F^{-1}(\bar z):\ D_N^*F(\bar y,\bar z)(0)\cap\ker D_N^*G(\bar x,\bar y)=\{0\}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\circ G\text{ is SNC at }(\bar x,\bar z)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: SNC composition with a Lipschitz-like inner mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite dimensionality of \(Y\) and surjectivity of the outer derivative are required only for the stronger SNC conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar z\in(f\circ G)(\bar x)\) and fix \(\bar y\in G(\bar x)\cap f^{-1}(\bar z)\). Assume that \(G\) is locally Lipschitz-like around \((\bar x,\bar y)\), that \(f\) is strictly differentiable at \(\bar y\), and that \((x,z)\mapsto G(x)\cap f^{-1}(z)\) is inner semicontinuous at \((\bar x,\bar z,\bar y)\). Then \(f\circ G\) is PSNC at \((\bar x,\bar z)\). If, additionally, \(\dim Y<\infty\) and \(\nabla f(\bar y)\) is surjective, then \(f\circ G\) is SNC there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A locally Lipschitz-like inner mapping composed with a strictly differentiable outer mapping is PSNC under inner semicontinuity of intermediate points. It is SNC if the intermediate space is finite-dimensional and the outer derivative is surjective.

f\text{ is strictly differentiable at }\bar y
(x,z)\mapsto G(x)\cap f^{-1}(z)\text{ is inner semicontinuous at }(\bar x,\bar z,\bar y)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: SNC preservation under a strictly differentiable outer mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The PSNC implication does not require surjectivity; the stronger SNC implication does.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G:X\rightrightarrows Y\), \(f:Y\to Z\), and \(\bar z\in(f\circ G)(\bar x)\). Suppose that, for some \(\bar y\in G(\bar x)\cap f^{-1}(\bar z)\), the multifunction \((x,z)\mapsto G(x)\cap f^{-1}(z)\) is inner semicontinuous at \((\bar x,\bar z,\bar y)\), and that \(f\) is strictly differentiable at \(\bar y\). Then (i) PSNC of \(G\) at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) implies PSNC of \(f\circ G\) at \((\bar x,\bar z)\); and (ii) SNC of \(G\) at \((\bar x,\bar y)\), together with surjectivity of \(\nabla f(\bar y)\), implies SNC of \(f\circ G\) at \((\bar x,\bar z)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under inner semicontinuity of the intermediate-point mapping, composition with a strictly differentiable outer mapping preserves PSNC. Preservation of full SNC additionally requires a surjective derivative.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: SNEC preservation under an SNC/PSNC alternative and a singular-subdifferential coderivative qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g:X\to Y\) be continuous around \(\bar x\), set \(\bar y=g(\bar x)\), and let \(\varphi:Y\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be proper and lower semicontinuous around \(\bar y\). Assume either that \(g\) is PSNC at \(\bar x\) and \(\varphi\) is SNEC at \(\bar y\), or that \(g\) is SNC at \(\bar x\). If \(\partial^\infty\varphi(\bar y)\cap\ker D_N^*g(\bar x)=\{0\}\), then \(\varphi\circ g\) is SNEC at \(\bar x\). In particular, \(\varphi\circ g\) is SNEC at \(\bar x\) when \(\varphi\) is locally Lipschitzian around \(\bar y\) and \(g\) is continuous around and PSNC at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper lower-semicontinuous outer function composed with a continuous mapping is SNEC under the stated SNC/PSNC alternative and singular-subdifferential coderivative qualification. Local Lipschitz continuity of the outer function yields the stated special case.
assumptions_latex: g:X\to Y\text{ is continuous around }\bar x
\varphi:Y\to\overline{\mathbb R}\text{ is proper and l.s.c. around }\bar y
\big(g\text{ is PSNC at }\bar x\text{ and }\varphi\text{ is SNEC at }\bar y\big)\lor\big(g\text{ is SNC at }\bar x\big)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \varphi\circ g\text{ is SNEC at }\bar x

knowledge_statements.statement_title: PSNC preservation under composition of set-valued mappings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composition rule requiring inner semicompactness of intermediate points, a disjunctive PSNC/SNC hypothesis, and a mixed-coderivative qualification at every reference intermediate point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let G:X\rightrightarrows Y, F:Y\rightrightarrows Z, and \bar z\in(F\circ G)(\bar x). Suppose G and F^{-1} are closed-graph near \bar x and \bar z, respectively, and S(x,z):=G(x)\cap F^{-1}(z) is inner semicompact at (\bar x,\bar z). If, for every \bar y\in S(\bar x,\bar z), either G is PSNC at (\bar x,\bar y) and F is PSNC at (\bar y,\bar z), or G is SNC at (\bar x,\bar y), and D_M^*F(\bar y,\bar z)(0)\cap\ker D_N^*G(\bar x,\bar y)=\{0\}, then F\circ G is PSNC at (\bar x,\bar z).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The composition is PSNC when intermediate points are inner semicompact, the stated PSNC-or-SNC alternative holds at every intermediate point, and the mixed-coderivative kernel qualification is satisfied there.
assumptions_latex: G:X\rightrightarrows Y,\quad F:Y\rightrightarrows Z,\quad \bar z\in(F\circ G)(\bar x)
G\text{ and }F^{-1}\text{ are closed-graph near }\bar x\text{ and }\bar z\text{, respectively}
S(x,z):=G(x)\cap F^{-1}(z)\text{ is inner semicompact at }(\bar x,\bar z)
\forall\bar y\in S(\bar x,\bar z),\quad[(G\text{ is PSNC at }(\bar x,\bar y)\land F\text{ is PSNC at }(\bar y,\bar z))\lor G\text{ is SNC at }(\bar x,\bar y)]
\forall\bar y\in S(\bar x,\bar z),\quad D_M^*F(\bar y,\bar z)(0)\cap\ker D_N^*G(\bar x,\bar y)=\{0\}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\circ G\text{ is PSNC at }(\bar x,\bar z).

source_refs.locator: 3.3.1 Sequential Normal Compactness of Set Intersections and Inverse Images p. 341

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C:=\bigcap_{i=1}^m C_i\). Under the stated normal qualification and SNC assumptions, every limiting normal to the intersection admits a decomposition into limiting normals to the individual sets:
\[
N_C(\bar x)\subset N_{C_1}(\bar x)+\cdots+N_{C_m}(\bar x).
\]
Thus compactness of the entire collection is unnecessary: SNC for all but one constituent rules out the weak-star vanishing sequences that obstruct passage from approximate normals to an exact normal decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under normal qualification, SNC of all but one intersecting set suffices for the limiting-normal intersection rule.

children.title: Intersection Normal Calculus
children.top_down_role: Normal-cone calculus for intersections of constraint sets.

assumptions_latex: \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\subset\mathbb R^n\) are closed near \(\bar x\in\bigcap_i C_i\).
Whenever \(v_i\in N_{C_i}(\bar x)\) and \(\sum_i v_i=0\), one has \(v_i=0\) for all \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\cap_i C_i}(\bar x)\subset\sum_i N_{C_i}(\bar x)\).

source_refs.locator: 3.1.1 Calculus of Normal Cones p. 262

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Set \(C:=\bigcap_{i=1}^m C_i\). If the only balanced family of limiting normals \(v_i\in N_{C_i}(\bar x)\) satisfying \(\sum_i v_i=0\) is the zero family, then
\[
N_C(\bar x)\subset N_{C_1}(\bar x)+\cdots+N_{C_m}(\bar x).
\]
Equivalently, every \(v\in N_C(\bar x)\) can be written as \(v=\sum_i v_i\) with \(v_i\in N_{C_i}(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Qualified limiting normals to a finite intersection decompose as sums of normals to its constituent sets.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regular and Exact Intersection Normal Rules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconditional regular-normal inclusion and the exact normally regular specialization for finite intersections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C:=\bigcap_{i=1}^m C_i\) and \(\bar x\in C\). Then
\[
\widehat N_{C_1}(\bar x)+\cdots+\widehat N_{C_m}(\bar x)\subset\widehat N_C(\bar x).
\]
If the sets are locally closed and normally regular at \(\bar x\), and
\[
v_i\in N_{C_i}(\bar x),\quad \sum_{i=1}^m v_i=0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad v_1=\cdots=v_m=0,
\]
then
\[
\widehat N_C(\bar x)=N_C(\bar x)=N_{C_1}(\bar x)+\cdots+N_{C_m}(\bar x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constituent regular normals always sum to a regular normal of the intersection; constituent normal regularity and transversality make the regular and limiting formulas exact.
assumptions_latex: For exactness, the sets are locally closed and normally regular at \(\bar x\), and the no-cancellation qualification holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_i\widehat N_{C_i}(\bar x)\subset\widehat N_C(\bar x)\), with equality of the regular and limiting formulas under the additional assumptions.
knowledge_statements.title: Regular and Exact Intersection Normal Rules

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite intersections of locally closed, possibly nonconvex subsets of Euclidean space under a normal qualification condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega_1,\ldots,\Omega_s\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty and locally closed around a common point \(\bar x\). If \(x_i\in N(\bar x;\Omega_i)\) for every \(i\) and \(\sum_{i=1}^s x_i=0\) imply \(x_i=0\) for every \(i\), then \[N\!\left(\bar x;\bigcap_{i=1}^s\Omega_i\right)\subseteq\sum_{i=1}^sN(\bar x;\Omega_i).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finitely many nonempty sets locally closed near a common point, if their limiting normals admit no nontrivial selection summing to zero, then every limiting normal to their intersection at that point is a sum of limiting normals to the individual sets.
assumptions_latex: \Omega_i\subset\mathbb{R}^n\text{ is nonempty and locally closed around }\bar x\in\bigcap_{i=1}^s\Omega_i
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N\!\left(\bar x;\bigcap_{i=1}^s\Omega_i\right)\subseteq\sum_{i=1}^sN(\bar x;\Omega_i)

children.top_down_role: Normal-cone calculus for preimages under mappings.

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\), and \(C\subset\mathbb R^m\) is closed near \(F(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{F^{-1}(C)}(\bar x)\subset \nabla F(\bar x)^*N_C(F(\bar x))\).

notation.meaning: adjoint of the derivative of the mapping

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional preimage rule with the standard normal qualification.

source_refs.locator: 3.1.1 Calculus of Normal Cones p. 262
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D:=F^{-1}(C)\). If no nonzero normal \(y^*\in N_C(F(\bar x))\) is annihilated by \(\nabla F(\bar x)^*\), then
\[
N_D(\bar x)\subset \nabla F(\bar x)^*N_C(F(\bar x)).
\]
Consequently, each \(x^*\in N_D(\bar x)\) has the form \(x^*=\nabla F(\bar x)^*y^*\) for some \(y^*\in N_C(F(\bar x))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the normal qualification, a preimage normal is the adjoint derivative applied to a normal of the target set.
knowledge_statements.title: Inverse-Image Normal Calculus

source_witnesses.locator: 3.1.1 Calculus of Normal Cones p. 262
source_witnesses.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regular-normal lower pullback and exactness under target normal regularity and the standard qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D:=F^{-1}(C)\) and \(\bar x\in D\). If \(F\) is differentiable at \(\bar x\), then
\[
\nabla F(\bar x)^*\widehat N_C(F(\bar x))\subset\widehat N_D(\bar x).
\]
If, additionally, \(F\) is continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\), \(C\) is locally closed and normally regular at \(F(\bar x)\), and
\[
N_C(F(\bar x))\cap\ker\nabla F(\bar x)^*=\{0\},
\]
then \(D\) is normally regular at \(\bar x\) and
\[
\widehat N_D(\bar x)=N_D(\bar x)=\nabla F(\bar x)^*N_C(F(\bar x)).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Target regular normals always pull back through the adjoint derivative; target normal regularity and the normal qualification make the regular and limiting formulas exact.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is differentiable at \(\bar x\), \(C\subset\mathbb R^m\), and \(D:=F^{-1}(C)\).
For exactness, \(F\) is continuously differentiable nearby, \(C\) is locally closed and normally regular at \(F(\bar x)\), and the adjoint-kernel qualification holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla F(\bar x)^*\widehat N_C(F(\bar x))\subset\widehat N_D(\bar x)\), with exact regular and limiting pullback formulas under the additional assumptions.
knowledge_statements.title: Regular and Exact Inverse-Image Pullback

children.title: Product-Set Normal Calculus
children.top_down_role: Normal-cone behavior for Cartesian product constructions.

assumptions_latex: \(C_i\subset\mathbb R^{n_i}\) is locally closed at \(\bar x_i\in C_i\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{C_1\times\cdots\times C_m}(\bar x_1,\ldots,\bar x_m)=\prod_i N_{C_i}(\bar x_i)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-product formula for limiting normal cones.

source_refs.locator: 1.1.3 Calculus of Generalized Normals p. 18
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(C:=C_1\times\cdots\times C_m\) and \(\bar x:=(\bar x_1,\ldots,\bar x_m)\), the limiting normal cone separates componentwise:
\[
N_C(\bar x)=N_{C_1}(\bar x_1)\times\cdots\times N_{C_m}(\bar x_m).
\]
Hence \((v_1,\ldots,v_m)\) is normal to the product at \(\bar x\) exactly when \(v_i\in N_{C_i}(\bar x_i)\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The limiting normal cone to a finite Cartesian product is exactly the product of the factor normal cones.
knowledge_statements.title: Product-Set Normal Calculus

source_witnesses.locator: 1.1.3 Calculus of Generalized Normals p. 18
source_witnesses.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regular and Clarke counterparts of the exact finite-product limiting-normal formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(C:=C_1\times\cdots\times C_m\) and \(\bar x:=(\bar x_1,\ldots,\bar x_m)\),
\[
\widehat N_C(\bar x)=\widehat N_{C_1}(\bar x_1)\times\cdots\times\widehat N_{C_m}(\bar x_m).
\]
In the finite-dimensional locally closed setting,
\[
N_C^C(\bar x)=N_{C_1}^C(\bar x_1)\times\cdots\times N_{C_m}^C(\bar x_m).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regular and Clarke normal cones to a finite Cartesian product factor exactly into the corresponding factor normal cones.
assumptions_latex: For the Clarke formula, the factors are finite-dimensional and locally closed at their reference points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regular and Clarke normal cones, like the limiting normal cone in the seed, factor exactly over the finite Cartesian product.
knowledge_statements.title: Regular and Clarke Product-Normal Formulas

children.title: Image-Set Normal Calculus
children.top_down_role: Normal-cone behavior for sets transported through mappings.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) is locally closed at \(\bar x\in C\).
\(A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) is an invertible linear mapping.

notation.meaning: inverse adjoint of an invertible linear mapping

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact image rule restricted to invertible linear coordinate transformations.

source_refs.locator: 1.1.3 Calculus of Generalized Normals p. 18
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D:=A(C)\) and \(\bar y:=A\bar x\). Then the limiting normal cone transforms contragrediently:
\[
N_D(\bar y)=A^{-*}N_C(\bar x).
\]
Equivalently, \(y^*\in N_D(A\bar x)\) if and only if \(A^*y^*\in N_C(\bar x)\). Invertibility makes this an exact image formula, with no multiplier ambiguity or image-closure qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under an invertible linear image, limiting normals transform by the inverse adjoint.
knowledge_statements.title: Image-Set Normal Calculus

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Normal Transport under a Local Diffeomorphism
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact local image-normal formula under a smooth change of coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Phi\) be a \(C^1\) diffeomorphism between neighborhoods of \(\bar x\) and \(\bar y:=\Phi(\bar x)\). Then
\[
\widehat N_{\Phi(C)}(\bar y)=\nabla\Phi(\bar x)^{-*}\widehat N_C(\bar x),
\qquad
N_{\Phi(C)}(\bar y)=\nabla\Phi(\bar x)^{-*}N_C(\bar x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local smooth change of coordinates transports regular and limiting normals by the inverse adjoint derivative.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) is locally closed at \(\bar x\in C\).
\(\Phi\) is a \(C^1\) diffeomorphism between neighborhoods of \(\bar x\) and \(\bar y:=\Phi(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat N_{\Phi(C)}(\bar y)=\nabla\Phi(\bar x)^{-*}\widehat N_C(\bar x)\) and \(N_{\Phi(C)}(\bar y)=\nabla\Phi(\bar x)^{-*}N_C(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Normal Transport under a Local Diffeomorphism

children.top_down_role: Normal-cone behavior across finite unions and active branches.

assumptions_latex: \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\subset\mathbb R^n\) are locally closed at \(\bar x\in C:=\bigcup_i C_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_C(\bar x)\subset\bigcup_{i:\,\bar x\in C_i}N_{C_i}(\bar x)\).

notation.meaning: active indices at the reference point

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-sided limiting-normal rule for a finite union of locally closed sets.

source_refs.locator: 1.1.3 Calculus of Generalized Normals p. 18
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the finite union \(C:=\bigcup_{i=1}^m C_i\), every limiting normal at \(\bar x\) is a limiting normal to at least one active constituent:
\[
N_C(\bar x)\subset\bigcup_{i\in I(\bar x)}N_{C_i}(\bar x),
\qquad I(\bar x):=\{i:\bar x\in C_i\}.
\]
The reverse inclusion need not hold when several constituents meet, because enlarging a set can remove normals carried by an individual branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A limiting normal to a finite union belongs to the normal cone of some active constituent; equality need not hold.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Union Normal Calculus

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regular Normals to a Finite Union
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact active-branch formula for regular normals to a finite locally closed union.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C:=\bigcup_{i=1}^m C_i\), \(\bar x\in C\), and \(I(\bar x):=\{i:\bar x\in C_i\}\). If the branches are closed relative to a common neighborhood of \(\bar x\), then
\[
\widehat N_C(\bar x)=\bigcap_{i\in I(\bar x)}\widehat N_{C_i}(\bar x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The regular normal cone to a finite union is the intersection of the regular normal cones of all active branches.
assumptions_latex: \(C=\bigcup_{i=1}^m C_i\subset\mathbb R^n\), \(\bar x\in C\), and the branches are closed relative to a common neighborhood of \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat N_C(\bar x)=\bigcap_{i\in I(\bar x)}\widehat N_{C_i}(\bar x)\).

children.top_down_role: Conditions and failure regimes specific to product, image, or union constructions.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{C\cap D}(\bar z)\not\subset N_C(\bar z)+N_D(\bar z)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tangential intersection demonstrates failure when the normal qualification is removed.

source_refs.locator: 3.1.1 Calculus of Normal Cones p. 262
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Here \(C\cap D=\{\bar z\}\), so \(N_{C\cap D}(\bar z)=\mathbb R^2\). However,
\[
N_C(\bar z)=\{(0,\beta):\beta\le0\},\qquad
N_D(\bar z)=\{(0,\beta):\beta\ge0\},
\]
and their sum is only \(\{0\}\times\mathbb R\). Thus the intersection normal rule fails without qualification. Indeed, nonzero opposite normals exist, so \(N_C(\bar z)\cap[-N_D(\bar z)]\ne\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two tangential sets intersect only at the origin, whose full normal cone strictly exceeds the sum of their vertical normal cones.
knowledge_statements.title: Operation-Specific Qualification Boundaries

source_witnesses.locator: 3.1.1 Calculus of Normal Cones p. 262
source_witnesses.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Singular smooth image showing the boundary of inverse-adjoint normal transport.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C:=\mathbb R\) and \(\Phi(x):=x^2\). Then \(\Phi(C)=[0,\infty)\), and
\[
N_C(0)=\{0\},\qquad \nabla\Phi(0)=0,\qquad N_{\Phi(C)}(0)=\mathbb R_-.
\]
Thus the critical image has nonzero normals although the source has none; the inverse-adjoint image formula is undefined at the singular derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The squaring image of the real line acquires a nonzero boundary normal at zero although the source line has no nonzero normal.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If the singular subdifferentials satisfy
\[
\partial^\infty f(\bar x)\cap[-\partial^\infty g(\bar x)]=\{0\},

\[
\partial(f+g)(\bar x)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sum calculus for lower-semicontinuous extended-real-valued functions under a horizon-subdifferential qualification condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\},\ i=1,\ldots,m, be lower semicontinuous, let \bar{x}\in\bigcap_{i=1}^m\operatorname{dom}f_i, and set f=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i. children.top_down_role: Subdifferential behavior under positive, negative, or vanishing scalar factors.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is lower semicontinuous near \(\bar x\) and finite at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial(\lambda f)(\bar x)=\lambda\partial f(\bar x)\) and \(\partial^\infty(\lambda f)(\bar x)=\lambda\partial^\infty f(\bar x)\).

source_refs.locator: 1.3.4 Subdifferential Calculus in Banach Spaces p. 112
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Positive scalar multiplication commutes exactly with generalized differentiation:
\[
\partial(\lambda f)(\bar x)=\lambda\partial f(\bar x),
\qquad
\partial^\infty(\lambda f)(\bar x)=\lambda\partial^\infty f(\bar x).
\]
Thus \(v\in\partial(\lambda f)(\bar x)\) if and only if \(v=\lambda u\) for some \(u\in\partial f(\bar x)\). The restriction \(\lambda>0\) is essential for the limiting subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive rescaling multiplies both limiting and singular subdifferentials by the same scalar.
knowledge_statements.title: Scalar Rescaling Calculus

source_refs.locator: 1.3.4 Subdifferential Calculus in Banach Spaces p. 112
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(g(x):=f(x)+\langle a,x\rangle+b\). Since the added term has constant gradient \(a\),
\[
\partial g(\bar x)=\partial f(\bar x)+a,
\qquad
\partial^\infty g(\bar x)=\partial^\infty f(\bar x).
\]
Accordingly, \(v\in\partial g(\bar x)\) exactly when \(v-a\in\partial f(\bar x)\); the constant \(b\) affects neither subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding an affine functional translates the limiting subdifferential by its slope and leaves the singular subdifferential unchanged.
knowledge_statements.title: Affine Perturbation Calculus

children.title: Additive–Rescaling Degeneracy Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Loss of exactness or informativeness under degenerate algebraic changes.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial(\lambda f)(0)\ne\lambda\partial f(0)\), and \(\partial(\delta_C+\delta_D)(\bar z)\not\subset\partial\delta_C(\bar z)+\partial\delta_D(\bar z)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failures for negative scaling and an unqualified indicator-function sum.

source_refs.locator: 3.2 Subdifferential Calculus and Related Topics p. 296
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Negative homogeneity fails because
\[
\partial f(0)=\{-1,1\},\qquad
\partial(-f)(0)=[-1,1]\ne-\partial f(0).
\]
Additive calculus can also fail without singular qualification. Since \(C\cap D=\{\bar z\}\), one has \(\partial(\delta_C+\delta_D)(\bar z)=\mathbb R^2\), whereas
\[
\partial\delta_C(\bar z)+\partial\delta_D(\bar z)=\{0\}\times\mathbb R.
\]
Thus positive scaling and the singular sum qualification mark genuine boundaries of the algebraic rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negative scaling can enlarge a limiting subdifferential, while failure of singular qualification can invalidate the subdifferential sum inclusion.
knowledge_statements.title: Additive–Rescaling Degeneracy Boundaries

children.top_down_role: Subdifferential behavior for scalar outer functions applied to inner functions.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\).
\(\phi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is continuously differentiable near \(f(\bar x)\), with \(\phi'(f(\bar x))>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial(\phi\circ f)(\bar x)=\phi'(f(\bar x))\partial f(\bar x)\).

source_refs.locator: 1.3.4 Subdifferential Calculus in Banach Spaces p. 112
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(h:=\phi\circ f\) and \(\alpha:=\phi'(f(\bar x))>0\). Then the limiting subdifferential obeys the exact scalar chain rule
\[
\partial h(\bar x)=\alpha\,\partial f(\bar x).
\]
Equivalently, \(v\in\partial(\phi\circ f)(\bar x)\) exactly when \(v=\phi'(f(\bar x))u\) for some \(u\in\partial f(\bar x)\). Positivity avoids the failure of negative homogeneity for nonregular limiting subdifferentials.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth scalar outer function with positive derivative scales the inner function’s limiting subdifferential exactly.
knowledge_statements.title: Scalar Composition Subdifferentials

source_witnesses.locator: 1.3.4 Subdifferential Calculus in Banach Spaces p. 112

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sign-reversed scalar chain representation and failure of naive negative homogeneity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\alpha=\phi'(f(\bar x))<0\) and define \(\partial^+f(\bar x):=-\partial(-f)(\bar x)\). Then
\[\partial(\phi\circ f)(\bar x)=\alpha\,\partial^+f(\bar x).\]
The ordinary limiting subdifferential cannot generally replace \(\partial^+f\): for \(f(x)=-|x|\) and \(\phi(t)=-t\),
\[\partial(\phi\circ f)(0)=[-1,1]\supsetneq\phi'(0)\partial f(0)=\{-1,1\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative outer derivative scales the upper limiting subdifferential; naive negative scaling of the lower limiting subdifferential can be strict.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\).
\(\phi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is continuously differentiable near \(f(\bar x)\), with \(\alpha=\phi'(f(\bar x))<0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\partial(\phi\circ f)(\bar x)=\alpha\,\partial^+f(\bar x).\]

\[\partial(\phi\circ f)(\bar x)=\{0\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero outer derivative makes the locally Lipschitz composite strictly differentiable with zero subdifferential.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\).
\(\phi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is continuously differentiable near \(f(\bar x)\).

\(g:\mathbb R^m\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is finite at \(\bar y=F(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\nabla F(\bar x)^\top\widehat\partial g(\bar y)\subseteq\widehat\partial(g\circ F)(\bar x).\]
knowledge_statements.title: Regular-Subgradient Pullback

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Horizon counterpart of the finite-dimensional qualified smooth-inner chain rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the horizon-kernel qualification,
\[\partial^\infty(g\circ F)(\bar x)\subseteq\nabla F(\bar x)^\top\partial^\infty g(F(\bar x)).\]
If \(g\) is locally Lipschitz at \(F(\bar x)\), both horizon subdifferentials equal \(\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The qualified smooth-inner rule also pulls back horizon subgradients; local Lipschitz continuity makes this formula trivial.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\).
\(g:\mathbb R^m\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is proper and lower semicontinuous near \(\bar y=F(\bar x)\), with \(g(\bar y)<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\partial^\infty(g\circ F)(\bar x)\subseteq\nabla F(\bar x)^\top\partial^\infty g(\bar y).\]
knowledge_statements.title: Horizon Chain Inclusion

children.title: Chain-Calculus Qualifications
children.top_down_role: Regularity conditions supporting informative composite estimates.

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is differentiable at \(\bar x\), and \(g:\mathbb{R}^m\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) is proper and lower semicontinuous at \(F(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\partial^\infty g(F(\bar x))\cap\ker \nabla F(\bar x)^\top=\{0\}.\]

notation.meaning: Horizon subdifferential of the outer function

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic horizon qualification excluding abnormal outer subgradients annihilated by the inner derivative.

source_refs.locator: 1.1.3 Calculus of Generalized Normals p. 18
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The basic chain-calculus qualification at \(\bar x\) is \[\partial^\infty g(F(\bar x))\cap\ker \nabla F(\bar x)^\top=\{0\}.\] Equivalently, no nonzero horizon subgradient of the outer function is annihilated by the adjoint derivative of the inner mapping. This condition suppresses abnormal normals in the inverse-image calculus underlying the limiting-subdifferential chain rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The qualification requires every outer horizon subgradient killed by the adjoint Jacobian to be zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Chain-Calculus Qualifications

source_witnesses.locator: 1.1.3 Calculus of Generalized Normals p. 18
source_witnesses.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

assumptions_latex: Either \(g\) is locally Lipschitz near \(F(\bar x)\), or \(\nabla F(\bar x):\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is surjective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\partial^\infty g(F(\bar x))\cap\ker\nabla F(\bar x)^\top=\{0\}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two standard sufficient conditions making the horizon-kernel qualification automatic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The condition \[\partial^\infty g(F( ar x))\cap\ker
abla F( ar x)^	op=\{0\}\] holds automatically if either (i) \(g\) is locally Lipschitz near \(F( ar x)\), so \(\partial^\infty g(F( ar x))=\{0\}\), or (ii) \(
abla F( ar x)\) is surjective, so \(\ker
abla F( ar x)^	op=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local Lipschitz continuity of the outer function or surjectivity of the inner Jacobian makes the chain qualification automatic.
knowledge_statements.title: Automatic Chain Qualification Regimes

children.title: Composition Exactness Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes separating exact composite calculus from one-sided estimates.

assumptions_latex: \(g:\mathbb{R}^m\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\partial(g\circ F)(\bar x)=A^\top\partial g(A\bar x+b).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact convex-affine boundary separating equality from the general limiting chain inclusion.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 1. Generalized Differentiation in Banach Spaces p. 3
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the convex-affine composition \(h(x)=g(Ax+b)\), the relative-interior qualification \(\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}g)\cap(A\mathbb{R}^n+b)\ne\varnothing\) yields the exact formula \[\partial h(\bar x)=A^\top\partial g(A\bar x+b)\] at every \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}h\). For a nonlinear inner mapping or a nonconvex outer function, the corresponding limiting-subdifferential rule generally provides only an inclusion unless additional regularity is imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexity, affine composition, and a relative-interior qualification give equality; general nonlinear nonconvex compositions usually give only inclusion.
knowledge_statements.title: Composition Exactness Boundaries

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 1. Generalized Differentiation in Banach Spaces p. 3
source_witnesses.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strictness of the qualified limiting chain inclusion for a Lipschitz piecewise-linear outer function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F(x)=(x,-x)\) and \(g(y_1,y_2)=\min\{y_1,y_2,0\}\), the outer function is globally Lipschitz, so the horizon qualification is automatic. At the origin,
\[\partial g(0,0)=\{(1,0),(0,1),(0,0)\},\qquad (g\circ F)(x)=-|x|,\]
and hence
\[\partial(g\circ F)(0)=\{-1,1\}\subsetneq\nabla F(0)^\top\partial g(0,0)=\{-1,0,1\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even under an automatic Lipschitz qualification, the limiting chain inclusion can be strict.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\partial(g\circ F)(0)=\{-1,1\}\subsetneq\nabla F(0)^\top\partial g(0,0)=\{-1,0,1\}.\]
knowledge_statements.title: Strict Qualified Chain Inclusion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact smooth-inner chain rule obtained when the outer function is subdifferentially regular and the standard horizon qualification holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(g\) is subdifferentially regular at \(\bar y=F(\bar x)\) and \(\partial^\infty g(\bar y)\cap\ker\nabla F(\bar x)^\top=\{0\}\), then \(g\circ F\) is subdifferentially regular at \(\bar x\) and
\[\widehat\partial(g\circ F)(\bar x)=\partial(g\circ F)(\bar x)=\nabla F(\bar x)^\top\partial g(\bar y).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Outer subdifferential regularity and the horizon-kernel qualification turn the smooth-inner limiting chain inclusion into equality.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\).
\(g:\mathbb R^m\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is proper and lower semicontinuous near \(\bar y=F(\bar x)\), finite and subdifferentially regular at \(\bar y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\widehat\partial(g\circ F)(\bar x)=\partial(g\circ F)(\bar x)=\nabla F(\bar x)^\top\partial g(\bar y).\]
knowledge_statements.title: Regularity-Based Exact Chain Rule

children.title: Active-Piece Extremum Calculus
children.top_down_role: Subgradient calculus for active-piece and extremum constructions.

children.title: Maximum-Function Subdifferentials
children.top_down_role: Subgradient structures for pointwise maximum constructions.

knowledge_statements.title: Maximum-Function Subdifferentials
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite maximum of continuously differentiable functions; limiting and Clarke subdifferentials coincide at the reference point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(I(\bar x)=\{i:f_i(\bar x)=f(\bar x)\}\). Then \(f\) is locally Lipschitz and Clarke regular at \(\bar x\), and \[\partial f(\bar x)=\partial_C f(\bar x)=\operatorname{co}\{\nabla f_i(\bar x):i\in I(\bar x)\}.\] Thus its subgradients are exactly the convex combinations of gradients of active pieces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite maximum of continuously differentiable functions, the limiting and Clarke subdifferentials equal the convex hull of the active gradients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\partial f(\bar x)=\partial_C f(\bar x)=\operatorname{co}\{\nabla f_i(\bar x):i\in I(\bar x)\}.\]

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 1. Generalized Differentiation in Banach Spaces p. 3

assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and convex.
Each \(f_i\) is finite and continuous near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\partial f(\bar x)=\operatorname{co}\left(\bigcup_{i\in I(\bar x)}\partial f_i(\bar x)\right).\]

notation.meaning: Convex subdifferential, coinciding here with the limiting subdifferential

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact convex-subdifferential rule for a finite maximum of continuous convex pieces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_i:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), \(i=1,\ldots,r\), be proper convex functions that are finite and continuous near \(\bar x\), and set \(f:=\max_i f_i\). Then \[\partial f(\bar x)=\operatorname{co}\!\left(\bigcup_{i\in I(\bar x)}\partial f_i(\bar x)\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The subdifferential of a finite continuous convex maximum is the convex hull of the active pieces' subdifferentials.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Convex Maximum Rule

children.title: Minimum-Function Subdifferentials
children.top_down_role: Subgradient structures for pointwise minimum constructions.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\partial f(\bar x)\subseteq\{\nabla f_i(\bar x):i\in I(\bar x)\},\qquad \partial_C f(\bar x)=\operatorname{co}\{\nabla f_i(\bar x):i\in I(\bar x)\}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite smooth minimum, distinguishing limiting from Clarke subdifferentials.

source_refs.locator: 9.2 Global Algorithms Based on the min Function p. 852
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I(\bar x)=\{i:f_i(\bar x)=f(\bar x)\}\). The limiting subdifferential of the finite smooth minimum obeys \[\partial f(\bar x)\subseteq\{\nabla f_i(\bar x):i\in I(\bar x)\},\] while local Lipschitzness gives the Clarke formula \[\partial_C f(\bar x)=\operatorname{co}\{\nabla f_i(\bar x):i\in I(\bar x)\}.\] Unlike a maximum, a minimum need not be Clarke regular, so convexification can strictly enlarge its limiting subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth finite minimum has limiting subgradients among active gradients, while its Clarke subdifferential is their convex hull.
knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Function Subdifferentials

source_witnesses.locator: 9.2 Global Algorithms Based on the min Function p. 852
source_witnesses.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\widehat\partial f(0)=\varnothing,\qquad\partial f(0)=\{-1,1\},\qquad\partial_C f(0)=[-1,1].\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional example separating regular, limiting, and Clarke subdifferentials of a smooth finite minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=\min\{x,-x\}=-|x|\), \[\widehat\partial f(0)=\varnothing,\qquad \partial f(0)=\{-1,1\},\qquad \partial_C f(0)=[-1,1].\] Thus Clarke convexification strictly enlarges the limiting subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For minus absolute value, the regular subdifferential is empty, the limiting subdifferential consists of the two active slopes, and the Clarke subdifferential is their interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict Convexification for a Smooth Minimum
knowledge_statements.title: Strict Convexification for a Smooth Minimum

assumptions_latex: \(f_i\) is continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\widehat\partial f(\bar x)=\{g\}\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \nabla f_i(\bar x)=g\text{ for all }i\in I(\bar x);\quad\text{otherwise }\widehat\partial f(\bar x)=\varnothing.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact regular-subgradient characterization at a tie of smooth minimum pieces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f=\min_{1\le i\le r}f_i\), where every \(f_i\) is continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\). Then \[\widehat\partial f(\bar x)=\begin{cases}\{g\},&\nabla f_i(\bar x)=g\ \text{for every }i\in I(\bar x),\\\varnothing,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth finite minimum has a regular subgradient at a tie exactly when all active gradients coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regular Subdifferential of a Smooth Finite Minimum
knowledge_statements.title: Regular Subdifferential of a Smooth Finite Minimum

children.title: Active-Index Selection Calculus
children.top_down_role: Subgradient contributions associated with locally active pieces.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(f^+)'(\bar x;d)=\max_{i\in I^+(\bar x)}\langle\nabla f_i(\bar x),d\rangle,\qquad (f^-)'(\bar x;d)=\min_{i\in I^-(\bar x)}\langle\nabla f_i(\bar x),d\rangle.\]

notation.meaning: Active indices for the maximum or minimum

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional selection rule for finite differentiable extrema.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 1. Generalized Differentiation in Banach Spaces p. 3
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(I^+(\bar x)=\{i:f_i(\bar x)=f^+(\bar x)\}\) and \(I^-(\bar x)=\{i:f_i(\bar x)=f^-(\bar x)\}\), only active pieces determine first-order directional behavior. For every \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \[(f^+)'(\bar x;d)=\max_{i\in I^+(\bar x)}\langle\nabla f_i(\bar x),d\rangle,\qquad (f^-)'(\bar x;d)=\min_{i\in I^-(\bar x)}\langle\nabla f_i(\bar x),d\rangle.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The directional derivative of a finite maximum or minimum selects the largest or smallest directional slope among active pieces.
knowledge_statements.title: Active-Index Selection Calculus

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 1. Generalized Differentiation in Banach Spaces p. 3
source_witnesses.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Directional Selection of Persisting Active Indices
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary first-order selection of active pieces along a prescribed direction, with sufficiency under a strict active-slope winner.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[
I^+(\bar x;d):=\operatorname*{argmax}_{i\in I^+(\bar x)}\langle\nabla f_i(\bar x),d\rangle,
\qquad
I^-(\bar x;d):=\operatorname*{argmin}_{i\in I^-(\bar x)}\langle\nabla f_i(\bar x),d\rangle.
\]
If \(t_k\downarrow0\), \(d_k\to d\), and an index \(i\) is active for \(f^+\) at every \(\bar x+t_kd_k\), then \(i\in I^+(\bar x;d)\); analogously, persistence for \(f^-\) implies \(i\in I^-(\bar x;d)\). Conversely, if the corresponding directional argmax or argmin is a singleton, its index is uniquely active along every sufficiently small ray perturbation \(\bar x+t d'\) with \(d'\) sufficiently close to \(d\). No converse is asserted when extremal slopes tie.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A persisting active piece must attain the extremal active directional slope; a strict slope winner becomes the unique nearby active piece in that direction.
assumptions_latex: \(f_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(i=1,\ldots,r\), are differentiable at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Persistence implies membership in \(I^+(\bar x;d)\) or \(I^-(\bar x;d)\); a singleton directional selection is locally uniquely active along that direction.

notation.meaning: active maximum indices attaining the largest directional slope
active minimum indices attaining the smallest directional slope

knowledge_statements.title: Directional Selection of Persisting Active Indices

children.title: Extremum-Selection Qualification Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regularity and failure regimes governing active-piece calculus.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[f(x)=x,\qquad I(x)=\varnothing,\qquad \partial f(x)=\{1\}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonattainment boundary for extending finite active-index formulas to infinite families.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 1. Generalized Differentiation in Banach Spaces p. 3
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f_n(x)=x-1/n\), one has \[f(x)=\sup_{n\in\mathbb{N}}f_n(x)=x.\] No index attains this supremum, so \(I(x)=\varnothing\) for every \(x\), whereas \(\partial f(x)=\{1\}\). Consequently, an active-index subdifferential formula based only on attaining indices fails for infinite families unless attainment or an appropriate compactness and near-active-index condition is imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an unattained infinite supremum, the active set can be empty although the supremum has a nonempty subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.title: Extremum-Selection Qualification Boundaries

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 1. Generalized Differentiation in Banach Spaces p. 3

assumptions_latex: \(U\subset\mathbb R^n\) and \(\phi:T\times U\to\mathbb R\) is continuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\varnothing\ne I(x):=\operatorname*{argmax}_{t\in T}\phi(t,x),\qquad I(x)\text{ is compact}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compactness and continuity sufficient for attainment in an infinite maximum family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be compact and \(\phi:T\times U\to\mathbb R\) be continuous. For \(f(x):=\max_{t\in T}\phi(t,x)\), the active set \(I(x):=\{t\in T:\phi(t,x)=f(x)\}\) is nonempty and compact for every \(x\in U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous family indexed by a compact set attains its maximum, and its maximizing-index set is compact.
knowledge_statements.title: Compact-Index Attainment Regime

children.top_down_role: Subdifferential calculus for partial minimization and parameterized values.

children.title: Partial-Minimization Subdifferentials
children.top_down_role: Subdifferential behavior for marginal functions formed by eliminating variables.

assumptions_latex: \(\Phi:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^m\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\partial p(\bar x)=\{x^*:\exists\bar y\in S(\bar x)\text{ with }(x^*,0)\in\partial\Phi(\bar x,\bar y)\}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact convex subdifferential formula for an attained infimal projection.

source_refs.locator: 5.1 Nonlinear Programming-Based Value Functions p. 254

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(\bar y\in S(\bar x)\), a vector \(x^*\) is a convex subgradient of the marginal function exactly when the lifted vector has zero component in the minimized variable: \[x^*\in\partial p(\bar x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad(x^*,0)\in\partial\Phi(\bar x,\bar y).\] Equivalently, \[\partial p(\bar x)=\{x^*:\exists\bar y\in S(\bar x)\text{ with }(x^*,0)\in\partial\Phi(\bar x,\bar y)\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subgradient of an attained convex marginal value lifts exactly to a joint subgradient whose minimized-variable component is zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Minimization Subdifferentials

source_witnesses.locator: 5.1 Nonlinear Programming-Based Value Functions p. 254

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional limiting and horizon upper estimates for a locally uniformly level-bounded infimal projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S(\bar x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_y\Phi(\bar x,y)\). Then
\[\partial p(\bar x)\subseteq\bigcup_{\bar y\in S(\bar x)}\{x^*:(x^*,0)\in\partial\Phi(\bar x,\bar y)\},\]
\[\partial^\infty p(\bar x)\subseteq\bigcup_{\bar y\in S(\bar x)}\{x^*:(x^*,0)\in\partial^\infty\Phi(\bar x,\bar y)\}.\]
Unlike the convex seed formula, these are generally only upper estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every limiting or horizon subgradient of a locally level-bounded marginal value lifts at some active minimizer with zero eliminated-variable component.
assumptions_latex: \(\Phi:\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is proper and lower semicontinuous.
\(\Phi\) is level-bounded in \(y\) locally uniformly in \(x\) at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\partial p(\bar x)\subseteq\bigcup_{\bar y\in S(\bar x)}\{x^*:(x^*,0)\in\partial\Phi(\bar x,\bar y)\},\quad \partial^\infty p(\bar x)\subseteq\bigcup_{\bar y\in S(\bar x)}\{x^*:(x^*,0)\in\partial^\infty\Phi(\bar x,\bar y)\}.\]
knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Infimal-Projection Inclusions

children.title: Value-Function Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: First-order sensitivity information encoded by parameterized optimal values.

assumptions_latex: \(Y\subset\mathbb{R}^m\) is compact, and \(\Phi:\mathbb{R}^n\times Y\to\mathbb{R}\) is continuous.
\(\nabla_x\Phi\) exists and is continuous near \(\{\bar x\}\times Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[p'(\bar x;d)=\min_{y\in S(\bar x)}\langle\nabla_x\Phi(\bar x,y),d\rangle.\]

notation.meaning: Directional derivative of the value function

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Danskin directional sensitivity for fixed compact decision sets.

source_refs.locator: 5.1 Nonlinear Programming-Based Value Functions p. 254

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The compactness and continuity assumptions make \(S(\bar x)\) nonempty. For every direction \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n\), the value function is directionally differentiable and satisfies \[p'(\bar x;d)=\min_{y\in S(\bar x)}\langle\nabla_x\Phi(\bar x,y),d\rangle.\] Hence first-order value sensitivity depends only on parameter gradients evaluated at solutions, with the direction selecting the smallest active slope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The directional derivative of a compactly parameterized minimum is the smallest parameter-direction slope among its active minimizers.
knowledge_statements.title: Value-Function Sensitivity

source_witnesses.locator: 5.1 Nonlinear Programming-Based Value Functions p. 254

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-gradient coincidence criterion for differentiability of a compactly parameterized minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If there is \(a\in\mathbb R^n\) such that
\[\nabla_x\Phi(\bar x,y)=a\qquad(y\in S(\bar x)),\]
then \(p\) is differentiable at \(\bar x\) and \(\nabla p(\bar x)=a\). A unique active minimizer is a sufficient special case.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coincidence of all active parameter gradients makes the value function differentiable with that common gradient.
assumptions_latex: The compactness and smoothness assumptions of the minimum-form Danskin theorem hold at \(\bar x\).
There exists \(a\in\mathbb R^n\) with \(\nabla_x\Phi(\bar x,y)=a\) for all \(y\in S(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[p\text{ is differentiable at }\bar x,\qquad \nabla p(\bar x)=a.\]
knowledge_statements.title: Active-Gradient Differentiability Criterion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clarke aggregation of active parameter gradients for a compactly parameterized minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The value function is locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\), and
\[\partial_Cp(\bar x)=\operatorname{co}\{\nabla_x\Phi(\bar x,y):y\in S(\bar x)\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Clarke subdifferential of a compact smooth minimum is the convex hull of its active parameter gradients.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\subset\mathbb R^m\) is compact, and \(\Phi:\mathbb R^n\times Y\to\mathbb R\) is continuous.
\(\nabla_x\Phi\) exists and is continuous near \(\{\bar x\}\times Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\partial_Cp(\bar x)=\operatorname{co}\{\nabla_x\Phi(\bar x,y):y\in S(\bar x)\}.\]
knowledge_statements.title: Clarke Active-Gradient Formula

children.title: Solution-Map Contributions
children.top_down_role: The role of minimizing selections and solution mappings in marginal estimates.

knowledge_statements.title: Solution-Map Contributions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derivative contribution of a differentiable local solution-map selection and its disappearance under inner stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(s\) be a differentiable local selection of the solution map \(S\), and suppose \(p(x)=\Phi(x,s(x))\) near \( ar x\). Then \[
abla p( ar x)=
abla_x\Phi( ar x,s( ar x))+Ds( ar x)^	op
abla_y\Phi( ar x,s( ar x)).\] The second term is the contribution from movement of the selected solution. If \(
abla_y\Phi( ar x,s( ar x))=0\), then \[
abla p( ar x)=
abla_x\Phi( ar x,s( ar x)).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Along a differentiable local solution selection, its movement contributes the selection derivative times the inner gradient. Inner stationarity removes this term and yields the envelope identity.
assumptions_latex: \(U\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is an open neighborhood of \(\bar x\), and \(S:U\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^m\) is a solution map.
\(s:U\to\mathbb{R}^m\) satisfies \(s(x)\in S(x)\) near \(\bar x\) and is differentiable at \(\bar x\).
\(\Phi:U\times\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}\) is differentiable at \((\bar x,s(\bar x))\), and \(p(x)=\Phi(x,s(x))\) near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[
abla p( ar x)=
abla_x\Phi( ar x,s( ar x))+Ds( ar x)^	op
abla_y\Phi( ar x,s( ar x)).\]

Value represented along the selected solution

children.title: Marginal Qualification Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Compactness, regularity, and attainment regimes controlling marginal calculus.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[p(0)=1,\qquad p(x)=0\text{ for }x\ne0,\qquad S(x)=\{1/x\}\text{ for }x\ne0.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by escaping minimizers and loss of local level boundedness.

source_refs.locator: 5.1 Nonlinear Programming-Based Value Functions p. 254

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\Phi(x,y)=(xy-1)^2\), direct minimization gives \[p(0)=1,\qquad p(x)=0\text{ for }x\ne0.\] Moreover, \(S(x)=\{1/x\}\) for \(x\ne0\), so minimizers escape to infinity as \(x\to0\). The value function is discontinuous at \(0\). Therefore smoothness of the integrand alone does not ensure marginal continuity or subdifferential sensitivity; local level boundedness, compactness, or an equivalent inner semicompactness condition is essential.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without local level boundedness, optimizers can escape to infinity and a smooth objective can produce a discontinuous marginal value.
knowledge_statements.title: Marginal Qualification Boundaries

source_witnesses.locator: 5.1 Nonlinear Programming-Based Value Functions p. 254

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal sequential compactness condition used to pass marginal subgradients through convergent active minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The argmin mapping \(S\) is value-attentively inner semicompact at \(\bar x\) if, whenever
\[x_k\to\bar x,\qquad p(x_k)\to p(\bar x),\qquad y_k\in S(x_k),\]
one can choose such minimizers so that a subsequence converges to some \(\bar y\in S(\bar x)\). Local uniform level-boundedness together with lower semicontinuity is a standard sufficient condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Marginal calculus needs convergent minimizing selections along value-attentive parameter sequences; local uniform level-boundedness is a convenient sufficient condition.
assumptions_latex: The sequences considered satisfy \(x_k\to\bar x\) and \(p(x_k)\to p(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\exists\,y_k\in S(x_k),\ k_j\uparrow\infty,\ \bar y\in S(\bar x):\quad y_{k_j}\to\bar y.\]
knowledge_statements.title: Attentive Inner Semicompactness of Minimizers

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compactness condition preventing bounded-value decisions from escaping near the reference parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The integrand is level-bounded in \(y\) locally uniformly in \(x\) at \(\bar x\) if, for every \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\), there are a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and a bounded set \(B\subset\mathbb R^m\) such that
\[\{y:\Phi(x,y)\le\alpha\}\subset B\qquad(x\in U).\]
For proper lower-semicontinuous \(\Phi\) with finite \(p(\bar x)\), this yields nonempty compact \(S(\bar x)\) and bounds every sequence \(y_k\) for which \(x_k\to\bar x\) and \(\sup_k\Phi(x_k,y_k)<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local uniform level-boundedness confines bounded-value decisions and yields compact attainment at the reference parameter.
assumptions_latex: \(\Phi:\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is proper and lower semicontinuous.
\(\Phi\) is level-bounded in \(y\) locally uniformly in \(x\) at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[S(\bar x)\ne\varnothing\text{ is compact},\qquad x_k\to\bar x,\ \sup_k\Phi(x_k,y_k)<\infty\Rightarrow (y_k)\text{ is bounded}.\]
knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Local Level-Boundedness

children.title: Integral-Functional Subdifferentiation

assumptions_latex: \((\Omega,\mathcal A,\mu)\) is a finite measure space, \(1\le p<\infty\), and \(q\) is conjugate to \(p\).
\(f:\Omega\times\mathbb{R}^d\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) is a convex normal integrand, and \(I(x)=\int_\Omega f(\omega,x(\omega))\,d\mu\).
\(I\) is finite and continuous at some point of \(L^p(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^d)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\partial I(x)=\{\xi\in L^q:\xi(\omega)\in\partial f(\omega,x(\omega))\text{ for almost every }\omega\}.\]

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x\in L^p(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^d)\) with \(I(x)<\infty\), a function \(\xi\in L^q(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^d)\) is a convex subgradient of \(I\) exactly when it is a measurable, integrable pointwise subgradient selection: \[\partial I(x)=\{\xi\in L^q(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^d):\xi(\omega)\in\partial f(\omega,x(\omega))\text{ for almost every }\omega\}.\] Thus subdifferentiation and integration interchange under the stated qualification.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fuzzy intersection rule for regular normals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nearby-point normal decomposition obtained from the extremal principle in the chapter's Asplund-space regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be an Asplund space, let \(\Omega_1,\Omega_2\subset X\) be locally closed around \(\bar x\in\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2\), and let \(x^*\in\widehat N(\bar x;\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2)\). For every \(\varepsilon>0\), there exist \(\lambda\geq0\), \(x_i\in\Omega_i\cap(\bar x+\varepsilon\mathbb B)\), and \(x_i^*\in\widehat N(x_i;\Omega_i)+\varepsilon\mathbb B^*\), \(i=1,2\), such that \(\lambda x^*=x_1^*+x_2^*\) and \(\max\{\lambda,\|x_1^*\|\}=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every tolerance, a regular normal to a locally closed two-set intersection admits a normalized decomposition into approximate regular normals at nearby points of the component sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Fuzzy Sum Rules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite fuzzy Fréchet-subdifferential sum rule in an Asplund space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i\). For every \(x^*\in\widehat\partial f(\bar x)\) and every \(\varepsilon>0\), there exist \(x_i\in B_\varepsilon(\bar x)\) and \(x_i^*\in\widehat\partial f_i(x_i)\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), such that \(|f_i(x_i)-f_i(\bar x)|<\varepsilon\) for every \(i\) and \(\|x^*-\sum_{i=1}^m x_i^*\|<\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every Fréchet subgradient of a finite sum can be approximated arbitrarily closely by a sum of Fréchet subgradients evaluated at nearby points with nearby component-function values.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is an Asplund space, and \(f_i:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), are lower semicontinuous near \(\bar x\in\bigcap_i\operatorname{dom}f_i\).
All but at most one of the functions \(f_i\) are locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(x^*\in\widehat\partial(\sum_{i=1}^m f_i)(\bar x)\) and every \(\varepsilon>0\), there exist points \(x_i\in B_\varepsilon(\bar x)\) and covectors \(x_i^*\in\widehat\partial f_i(x_i)\) such that \(|f_i(x_i)-f_i(\bar x)|<\varepsilon\) for every \(i\) and \(\|x^*-\sum_{i=1}^m x_i^*\|<\varepsilon\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate sum calculus for finitely many extended-real-valued functions using nearby value-compatible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f_1,\ldots,f_n:\mathbf E\to[-\infty,+\infty]\) be lower semicontinuous near \(z\in\mathbf E\). Then, for every \(\delta>0\),
\[
\partial_-\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^n f_i\right)(z)
\subseteq \delta B+\sum_{i=1}^n\partial_-f_i\bigl(U(f_i,z,\delta)\bigr),
\]
where \(B\) is the unit ball and \(\partial_-f_i(U)=\bigcup_{x\in U}\partial_-f_i(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every positive tolerance, each Dini subgradient of the finite sum lies in the sum of Dini subdifferentials evaluated at nearby value-compatible points, up to an error from the tolerance-scaled unit ball.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial_-\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^n f_i\right)(z)\subseteq\delta B+\sum_{i=1}^n\partial_-f_i\bigl(U(f_i,z,\delta)\bigr).

children.title: Fuzzy Chain Rules
children.top_down_role: Approximate subdifferential estimates for composite constructions.

assumptions_latex: \(X,Y\) are Asplund spaces, \(F:X\to Y\) is locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\), and \(g:Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is lower semicontinuous near \(F(\bar x)\).
The composition \(g\circ F\) is finite at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(x^*\in\widehat\partial(g\circ F)(\bar x)\) and \(\varepsilon>0\), there exist \(x\in B_\varepsilon(\bar x)\), \(y\in B_\varepsilon(F(\bar x))\), and \(y^*\in\widehat\partial g(y)\) such that \(|g(y)-g(F(\bar x))|<\varepsilon\) and \(x^*\in\widehat D^*F(x)(y^*)+\varepsilon B_{X^*}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Exactness Qualification Thresholds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: No-abnormal-cancellation qualification used when deriving exact limiting inclusions from fuzzy calculus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A standard qualification for a finite family excludes nontrivial singular cancellation: \[x_i^*\in\partial^\infty f_i(\bar x),\quad \sum_i x_i^*=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_1^*=\cdots=x_m^*=0.\] For two functions this condition is equivalent to \[\partial^\infty f_1(\bar x)\cap[-\partial^\infty f_2(\bar x)]=\{0\}.\] Analogous mapping qualifications use zero-input coderivative images. Additional compactness or sequential-normal-compactness assumptions may be required in infinite-dimensional limiting calculus.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A standard exact-calculus qualification rules out nontrivial cancellation among singular subgradients or zero-input coderivative elements; infinite-dimensional results may require additional compactness assumptions.
assumptions_latex: A candidate exact limiting-calculus rule is obtained by passing to the limit in a fuzzy Fréchet rule.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional limiting-coderivative estimate for a multifunction sum with decomposition compactness and explicit abnormal-multiplier exclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(x):=\sum_{i=1}^mF_i(x)\) and define the decomposition mapping
\[
\Xi(x,y):=\{(y_1,\ldots,y_m):y_i\in F_i(x),\ \sum_i y_i=y\}.
\]
Assume \(\Xi\) is inner semicompact at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) relative to its domain. Suppose that, for every \((\bar y_1,\ldots,\bar y_m)\in\Xi(\bar x,\bar y)\),
\[
x_i^*\in D^*F_i(\bar x,\bar y_i)(0),\quad \sum_i x_i^*=0
\Longrightarrow x_i^*=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).
\]
Then, for every \(y^*\in Y^*\),
\[
D^*F(\bar x,\bar y)(y^*)
\subset
\bigcup_{(\bar y_1,\ldots,\bar y_m)\in\Xi(\bar x,\bar y)}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(x):=\bigcap_{i=1}^mF_i(x)\), with \(\bar y\in F_i(\bar x)\) for every \(i\). Assume the graphs are locally closed and
\[
\left.\begin{array}{c}
x_i^*\in D^*F_i(\bar x,\bar y)(y_i^*),\quad i=1,\ldots,m,\\
\sum_i x_i^*=0,\qquad \sum_i y_i^*=0
\end{array}\right\}
\Longrightarrow (x_i^*,y_i^*)=(0,0)\ \text{for every }i.
\]
Then, for every \(y^*\in Y^*\),
\[
D^*F(\bar x,\bar y)(y^*)
\subset
\bigcup_{\sum_i y_i^*=y^*}
\sum_{i=1}^mD^*F_i(\bar x,\bar y)(y_i^*).
\]

\Longleftrightarrow

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) given by \(F(x)=x^2\), one has
\[
D^*F(0,0)(y^*)=\{0\}\quad\text{for every }y^*\in\mathbb R,
\]
so
\[
\{y^*:0\in D^*F(0,0)(y^*)\}=\mathbb R\neq\{0\}.
\]
The inverse satisfies \(F^{-1}(y)=\{-\sqrt y,\sqrt y\}\) for \(y>0\), and its branches are not Lipschitz at \(0\). Equivalently, the implicit equation \(x^2-y=0\) has no Aubin-stable solution localization at \((0,0)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the tangent-intersection hypothesis, for every \(u\in X\),
\[
DP(\bar x,(\bar y_1,\ldots,\bar y_m))(u)
=
DF_1(\bar x,\bar y_1)(u)\times\cdots\times DF_m(\bar x,\bar y_m)(u).
\]
For any set-valued mapping \(F:X\rightrightarrows Y\), coordinate exchange of its graph gives the unconditional inverse formula
\[
DF^{-1}(\bar y,\bar x)(v)
=
\{u\in X:v\in DF(\bar x,\bar y)(u)\}.
\]
Both identities follow directly from the corresponding contingent-tangent representations of the operation graphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under tangent compatibility, graphical derivatives commute with common-input products; inversion always exchanges the derivative input and output directions.
