children.title: Nonconvex Duality Gaps
children.top_down_role: Discrepancies between primal and dual values in nonconvex settings.

assumptions_latex: The primal problem is minimization subject to \(g(x)\le0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d\le p\), and the extended-real difference \(p-d\) is the Lagrangian duality gap whenever the values are defined without an indeterminate form.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General inequality-constrained minimization without convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[p:=\inf\{f(x):g(x)\le0\},\qquad q(\lambda):=\inf_x\bigl(f(x)+\langle\lambda,g(x)\rangle\bigr),\qquad d:=\sup_{\lambda\ge0}q(\lambda),\] weak duality gives \(d\le p\). When the extended-real difference is well-defined, \(p-d\) is the Lagrangian duality gap; the gap is strict when \(d<p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Lagrangian dual supplies a lower bound, and the difference between primal and dual values is the duality gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lagrangian Duality Gap and Weak Duality
knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Duality Gap and Weak Duality

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The problem is nonconvex but its primal and Lagrangian dual values both equal \(1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonconvexity permits but does not imply a positive Lagrangian duality gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R}x^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad(x^2-1)^2\le0,\] the feasible set is \(\{-1,1\}\), hence the problem is nonconvex. Nevertheless, its primal value and Lagrangian dual value are both \(1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A genuinely constrained nonconvex problem can still have zero Lagrangian duality gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonconvexity Does Not Force a Positive Gap
knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvexity Does Not Force a Positive Gap

assumptions_latex: \(v(u):=\inf\{f(x):g(x)\le u\}\) is a proper extended-real perturbation value function.
The Lagrangian uses multipliers \(\lambda\ge0\), so the dual variables for conjugacy are \(-\lambda\).

notation.meaning: Lower-semicontinuous convex biconjugate of the perturbation value

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lagrangian duality represented by the closed convex envelope of the perturbation value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[v(u):=\inf\{f(x):g(x)\le u\},\qquad p=v(0).\] For the standard nonnegative-multiplier Lagrangian, the dual value satisfies \[d=v^{**}(0).\] Hence \[p-d=v(0)-v^{**}(0).\] In particular, equality \(v(0)=v^{**}(0)\) eliminates the gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Lagrangian gap is the loss from replacing the perturbation value by its closed convex envelope at the reference perturbation.
knowledge_statements.title: Perturbation-Function Characterization of the Gap

assumptions_latex: The primal problem is \(\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ g(x)\le0\}\), with multipliers \(\lambda\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p=1\), \(d=\sup_{\lambda\ge0}\inf_{x\in X}(f(x)+\lambda g(x))=\tfrac12\), and \(p-d=\tfrac12\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A finite nonconvex problem with a strict Lagrangian duality gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The sole feasible point is \(x=0\), so the primal value is \(p=f(0)=1\). The Lagrangian dual function is \[q(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in\{0,1\}}\{f(x)+\lambda g(x)\}=\min\{1-\lambda,\lambda\},\qquad \lambda\ge0.\] Its maximum occurs at \(\lambda=\tfrac12\), giving \[d=\sup_{\lambda\ge0}q(\lambda)=\tfrac12<1=p.\] Hence weak duality holds, but nonconvexity permits the strict gap \(p-d=\tfrac12\); the dual value cannot certify the primal optimum exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-point nonconvex problem has primal value one and Lagrangian dual value one-half, producing a strict duality gap.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Duality Gaps

children.title: Saddle Certificate Failures
children.top_down_role: Regimes where differential information does not support a saddle interpretation.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in X}\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda}L(x,\lambda)=\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\inf_{x\in X}L(x,\lambda)=0\), but no \((\bar x,\bar\lambda)\) is a saddle point because the common value is not attained in \(\Lambda\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zero-gap convex-concave example showing that dual attainment is independently necessary for a saddle certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X=\{0\}\), \(\Lambda=[0,+\infty)\), and \(L(0,\lambda)=-e^{-\lambda}\), both minimax values equal \(0\). The multiplier slice is continuous and concave but has no maximizer on \(\Lambda\), so no saddle pair exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex-concave problem can have zero minimax gap but no saddle certificate because the dual supremum is not attained.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Gap Saddle Failure through Nonattainment

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No \((\bar x,\bar\lambda)\in X\times\Lambda\) satisfies \(L(\bar x,\lambda)\le L(\bar x,\bar\lambda)\le L(x,\bar\lambda)\) for all \((x,\lambda)\in X\times\Lambda\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict duality gap prevents existence of a primal-dual saddle certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x=0\), one has \(L(0,\lambda)=1-\lambda\), whose maximum over \(\lambda\ge0\) occurs at \(\lambda=0\); however, \(x=0\) does not minimize \(L(\cdot,0)\). For \(x=1\), one has \(L(1,\lambda)=\lambda\), which has no maximum on \(\Lambda\). Therefore neither primal point can participate in a saddle pair. Equivalently, the strict gap \(\sup_{\lambda\ge0}\inf_{x\in X}L(x,\lambda)=\tfrac12<1\) rules out any saddle certificate attaining the primal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In the finite gap example, neither primal point can form a saddle pair, so no saddle certificate recovers the primal optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Saddle Certificate Failures

children.title: Multiplier Certificate Failures
children.top_down_role: Regimes where multipliers fail to provide exact or informative certificates.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\bar x,\bar\lambda)=(0,0)\) satisfies KKT, but \(\bar x\) is a strict local maximum and is not a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of KKT sufficiency despite a valid multiplier tuple.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R}-x^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad x^2-1\le0,\] the pair \((\bar x,\bar\lambda)=(0,0)\) satisfies primal feasibility, dual feasibility, complementarity, and stationarity. Nevertheless, \(\bar x=0\) is a strict local maximum and is not a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonconvex problem can have a valid KKT multiplier at a strict local maximum.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: KKT Multipliers Need Not Certify Optimality in Nonconvex Problems
knowledge_statements.title: KKT Multipliers Need Not Certify Optimality in Nonconvex Problems

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible optimizer is unique, while the multiplier set \(\{(\mu_1,\mu_2):1+\mu_1+2\mu_2=0\}\) is infinite.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonuniqueness of equality multipliers under linearly dependent constraint gradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_x x\) subject to \(x=0\) and \(2x=0\), the unique feasible point is \(\bar x=0\), but its equality-multiplier set is \[\{(\mu_1,\mu_2):1+\mu_1+2\mu_2=0\},\] which is infinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Redundant constraints can leave a unique optimizer with infinitely many multiplier certificates.
knowledge_statements.title: Redundancy Destroys Multiplier Identifiability

assumptions_latex: A classical multiplier certificate requires \(\lambda\ge0\), stationarity, feasibility, and complementarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The unique feasible optimizer is \(\bar x=0\), but no \(\lambda\ge0\) satisfies \(1+2\lambda\bar x=0\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of multiplier existence when the active constraint has zero derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The constraint \(x^2\le0\) forces \(x=0\), so \(\bar x=0\) is the unique global minimizer. A KKT multiplier would have to satisfy \[0=f'(\bar x)+\lambda g'(\bar x)=1+2\lambda\bar x,\qquad \lambda\ge0,\qquad \lambda g(\bar x)=0.\] At \(\bar x=0\), stationarity reduces to \(0=1\), independently of \(\lambda\). Thus no multiplier certificate exists. The failure is caused by degeneracy of the active constraint, since \(g'(0)=0\), and illustrates why a constraint qualification is needed for multiplier necessity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A degenerate active constraint yields a unique optimizer but no KKT multiplier, demonstrating failure of multiplier certification without constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Certificate Failures

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the program \(\min_x f(x)\) subject to \(g_i(x)\le0\), Slater's condition and primal attainment imply the existence of \(\bar\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\) such that \[0\in\partial f(\bar x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\bar\lambda_i\partial g_i(\bar x),\qquad g_i(\bar x)\le0,\qquad \bar\lambda_i g_i(\bar x)=0.\] Moreover, \((\bar x,\bar\lambda)\) satisfies \[L(\bar x,\lambda)\le L(\bar x,\bar\lambda)\le L(x,\bar\lambda)\] for all \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\). Consequently, the dual optimum is attained and equals the primal optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an attained convex program satisfying Slater's condition, KKT multipliers exist, a saddle certificate holds, and the duality gap vanishes.
